title: Fix for pyright error
description:
This fixes the following pyright errors (https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/actions/runs/16580015762/job/46893662696):

```
pyright
/home/runner/work/py-shinylive/py-shinylive/shinylive/_main.py
  /home/runner/work/py-shinylive/py-shinylive/shinylive/_main.py:25:62 - error: Argument of type "object" cannot be assigned to parameter "invoke_without_command" of type "bool" in function "__init__"
    "object" is not assignable to "bool" (reportArgumentType)
  /home/runner/work/py-shinylive/py-shinylive/shinylive/_main.py:25:62 - error: Argument of type "object" cannot be assigned to parameter "no_args_is_help" of type "bool | None" in function "__init__"
    Type "object" is not assignable to type "bool | None"
      "object" is not assignable to "bool"
      "object" is not assignable to "None" (reportArgumentType)
  /home/runner/work/py-shinylive/py-shinylive/shinylive/_main.py:25:62 - error: Argument of type "object" cannot be assigned to parameter "subcommand_metavar" of type "str | None" in function "__init__"
    Type "object" is not assignable to type "str | None"
      "object" is not assignable to "str"
      "object" is not assignable to "None" (reportArgumentType)
  /home/runner/work/py-shinylive/py-shinylive/shinylive/_main.py:25:62 - error: Argument of type "object" cannot be assigned to parameter "chain" of type "bool" in function "__init__"
    "object" is not assignable to "bool" (reportArgumentType)
  /home/runner/work/py-shinylive/py-shinylive/shinylive/_main.py:25:62 - error: Argument of type "object" cannot be assigned to parameter "result_callback" of type "((...) -> Any) | None" in function "__init__"
    Type "object" is not assignable to type "((...) -> Any) | None"
      Type "object" is not assignable to type "(...) -> Any"
      "object" is not assignable to "None" (reportArgumentType)
5 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations 
make: *** [Makefile:52: pyright] Error 1
```


The error is new due to a change in the `Group.__init__` method from the `click` package.

In 8.1.8, it looked like this (https://github.com/pallets/click/blob/8.1.8/src/click/core.py#L1827-L1832):

```py
class Group(Command): 

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: t.Optional[str] = None,
        commands: t.Optional[
            t.Union[t.MutableMapping[str, Command], t.Sequence[Command]]
        ] = None,
        **attrs: t.Any,
    ) -> None:
```

In 8.2.0, it change to this, with some new named arguments (https://github.com/pallets/click/blob/8.2.0/src/click/core.py#L1513-L1525):

```py
class Group(Command): 

    def __init__(
        self,
        name: str | None = None,
        commands: cabc.MutableMapping[str, Command]
        | cabc.Sequence[Command]
        | None = None,
        invoke_without_command: bool = False,
        no_args_is_help: bool | None = None,
        subcommand_metavar: str | None = None,
        chain: bool = False,
        result_callback: t.Callable[..., t.Any] | None = None,
        **kwargs: t.Any,
    ) -> None:
```


I added those same named arguments to the new class. I think it should be fine with older versions of click -- it passes type checking with click 8.1.7 and the latest, 8.2.1.

Show status when downloading assets
description:
This change makes it so that the asset download status is printed, and updated every 1 second. This is helpful when on a not-super-fast internet connection so that the user has an idea what is happening and how long they will have to wait.

```
❯ shinylive assets download
Downloading https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/releases/download/v0.7.0/shinylive-0.7.0.tar.gz...
5%, 6604 KB/s, 20.4/343.6 MB
```

It adds an option `--no-status` to disable the displaying of the status. However, as of right now, that option is only available when running `shinylive assets download`. It's not there if you run `shinylive export ...` and the assets are automatically downloaded. I think that's OK, since I believe it would be an unusual case where someone wants to run `shinylive export` _and_ suppress the status, and for those use cases, they could just run `shinylive assets download --no-status` first.

title: feat: Update export command to use `--template-dir` and `--template-param`
description:
Pairs with https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/pull/144
Helps with https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/issues/110

This PR adds `template_dir` and `template_params` to `shinylive.export()` and as command line arguments in `shinylive export`.

* `template_dir` or `--template-dir` allows users to customize the `index.html` file used by the exported app. This argument takes a path that, effectively, supercedes the path in the shinylive assets.
* `template_params` or `--template-params` takes a dict of template parameters (in Python) or a JSON string or path to JSON in the CLI. https://github.com/posit-dev/shinylive/pull/144/files introduces a new set of template params, e.g. `{{ title }}`. This argument also covers parameters introduced by custom templates, or future parameters added to the default shinylive template.

We now also use [mustache](https://mustache.github.io/) for templating via chevron to render the templates. In addition to being a more powerful templating engine, this also allows us to use the same template logic for both R and Python. [chevron](https://pypi.org/project/chevron/) appears to be under-maintained but stable and recommended from [the mustache frontpage](https://mustache.github.io/).

Refactor: Shinylive URL encode/decode
description:
#20 introduced `shinylive url` commands and a set of functions to create and decode shinylive.io URLs. In practice, I've found the functions to be very helpful. But the functional design I used in #20 introduces some friction when I need to work with an app bundle and format it or manipulate it.

This PR refactors the shinylive.io url encoding and decoding to use a central `ShinyliveApp` class that implements a number of useful methods. This makes it much easier to use the app bundle built with `url_encode()` or `url_decode()` in a variety of settings and to produce several outputs from the same set of app files, without having to reach into the `shinylive._url` module.

As part of this, I renamed `encode_shinylive_url()` and `decode_shinylive_url()` to `url_encode()` and `url_decode()`, since they'll most often be called as `shinylive.url_encode()`.

`url_decode()` will now return a `ShinyliveApp`, while `url_encode()` still returns the Shinylive URL as a string.

The `ShinyliveApp` class implements:

* `.to_url()` to return the shinylive.io URL
* `.to_chunk_contents()` to create the shinylive chunk contents for a quarto shinylive chunk
* `.to_chunk()` to create a complete shinylive chunk, including the header and options, from the app
* `.to_json()` to return the JSON representation of the app bundle
* `.write_files()` to write the app bundle to a directory
* `.view()` to open the shinylive.io URL in a web browser

The `ShinyliveApp` constructor takes a ready-to-go app bundle of `list[FileContentJson]`, but most users will instead use class methods to construct the `ShinyliveApp` from various sources:

* `.from_url()` decodes a URL into a `ShinyliveApp`
* `.from_local()` creates a `ShinyliveApp` from a set of local files
* `.from_text()` creates a `ShinyliveApp` from a string with the contents of `app.py` or `app.R` (optionally with support of local `files`).

Once created, there are additional methods to help add to or remove from the app bundle. These methods all allow for method chaining.

* `.add_file()`, `add_files()` or `.add_file_contents()` (i.e. text files with a given name),
* `.remove_file()` to take a file, by name, out of the bundle. 

Additionally, I implemented `+` and `-` operators for the local app class to add and remove files from the bundle.

title: feat: Add `shinylive url` command
description:
Adds `shinylive url`, a command group to `encode` (or create) a shinylive.io URL for Python or R apps from local files or `decode` the existing URL. The core functionality is wrapped in `encode_shinylive_url()` and `decode_shinylive_url()` which are exported to facilitate creating and decoding shinylive URLs from within a Python session (the primary use case is for the Component and Layout galleries, but I'm sure this would be broadly useful).

```
❯ shinylive url encode --help
Usage: shinylive url encode [OPTIONS] APP [FILES]...

  Create a shinylive.io URL for a Shiny app from local files.

  APP is the path to the primary Shiny app file.

  FILES are additional supporting files or directories for the app.

  On macOS, you can copy the URL to the clipboard with:

      shinylive url encode app.py | pbcopy

Options:
  -m, --mode [editor|app]         The shinylive mode: include the editor or
                                  show only the app.  [required]
  -l, --language [python|py|R|r]  The primary language used to run the app, by
                                  default inferred from the app file.
  -v, --view                      Open the link in a browser.
  --no-header                     Hide the Shinylive header.
  --help                          Show this message and exit.
```

```
❯ shinylive url decode --help
Usage: shinylive url decode [OPTIONS] [URL]

  Decode a shinylive.io URL.

  URL is the shinylive editor or app URL. If not specified, the URL will be
  read from stdin, allowing you to read the URL from a file or the clipboard.

  On macOS, you can read the URL from the clipboard with:

      pbpaste | shinylive url decode

Options:
  --out TEXT  Output directory into which the app's files will be written. The
              directory is created if it does not exist.
  --json      Prints the decoded shinylive bundle as JSON to stdout, ignoring
              --out.
  --help      Show this message and exit.
```

## Examples

Copy the [multiple files Python app example link](https://shinylive.io/py/editor/#-DZ7BxllM5BJZO0FO5HAAVOgKODAsCIvDgaDwahaXQsLC4AgkciUMjUG6mVE-CCPEEhcGQkEggBUTFGEA5AF0gA):

```
pbpaste | shinylive url decode
```
```
## file: app.py

from shiny import App, render, ui
from utils import square

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_slider("n", "N", 0, 100, 20),
    ui.output_text_verbatim("txt"),
)


def server(input, output, session):
    @output
    @render.text
    def txt():
        val = square(input.n())
        return f"{input.n()} squared is {val}"


app = App(app_ui, server, debug=True)

## file: utils.py

def square(n):
    return n * n
```

Copy this example Shiny app

```python
from shiny import App, render, ui

app_ui = ui.page_fluid(
    ui.input_slider("x", "Slider input", min=0, max=20, value=10),
    ui.output_text_verbatim("txt"),
)


def server(input, output, session):
    @output
    @render.text
    def txt():
        return f"x: {input.x()}"


app = App(app_ui, server, debug=True)
```

and then generate a link and open it on shinylive

```
pbpaste | shinylive url encode --view
```

Try the same idea, but with this R app

```r
library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  h2(textOutput("currentTime"))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$currentTime <- renderText({
    invalidateLater(1000, session)
    paste("The current time is", Sys.time())
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

```
pbpaste | shinylive url encode --view
```

Or apply the same idea to a local app on your computer. In this case, the language is inferred from the file extension.

```
shinylive url encode -v posit-dev/py-shiny/examples/event/app.py

shinylive url encode -v rstudio/shiny/inst/examples/11_timer/app.R
```

title: Add fix to avoid tar path traversal
description: Cleaner alternative to #2. Fixes CVE-2007-4559.

title: CVE-2007-4559 Patch
description:
# Patching CVE-2007-4559

Hi, we are security researchers from the Advanced Research Center at [Trellix](https://www.trellix.com). We have began a campaign to patch a widespread bug named CVE-2007-4559. CVE-2007-4559 is a 15 year old bug in the Python tarfile package. By using extract() or extractall() on a tarfile object without sanitizing input, a maliciously crafted .tar file could perform a directory path traversal attack. We found at least one unsantized extractall() in your codebase and are providing a patch for you via pull request. The patch essentially checks to see if all tarfile members will be extracted safely and throws an exception otherwise. We encourage you to use this patch or your own solution to secure against CVE-2007-4559. Further technical information about the vulnerability can be found in this [blog](https://www.trellix.com/en-us/about/newsroom/stories/research/tarfile-exploiting-the-world.html).

If you have further questions you may contact us through this projects lead researcher [Kasimir Schulz](mailto:kasimir.schulz@trellix.com).

title: ci: Test on Python 3.14
description:
## Why

py-shinylive's CI matrix stopped at 3.13, while py-shiny and py-shinyswatch already test 3.14. That made py-shinylive the only package in the release train not exercised on the newest interpreter — and it's the one that wires the others together for `shinylive export`. Noticed while running the v1.7.0 release train.

## What

- `.github/workflows/build.yml`: add `"3.14"` to the build matrix
- `setup.cfg`: add the matching `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14` classifier, so the advertised support matches what's tested

`python_requires = >=3.10` is unchanged.

## Verification

Built and tested against 3.14 locally before asking CI to assert it:

```
$ python --version
Python 3.14.1
$ python -m pytest tests/ -q
13 passed
```

`import shinylive` resolves and reports version 0.8.11.

Follow-up to #63; part of the py-shiny v1.7.0 release train (see posit-dev/py-shiny#2377).

title: ci: Add reusable workflow to deploy an app to GitHub Pages
description:
## Summary

Ports [r-shinylive's `deploy-app` workflow](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/blob/main/.github/workflows/deploy-app.yaml) to Python, so a repo whose root is a Shiny app can publish it to GitHub Pages via a ~20-line caller workflow.

Matching the R package's layout:

- **`.github/workflows/deploy-app.yaml`** — the reusable (`workflow_call`) workflow. `astral-sh/setup-uv` + `uvx shinylive export <app-dir> site`, then `upload-pages-artifact` / `deploy-pages`. Upload and deploy are gated on `refs/heads/main`, so pull request events still build the site as a check without publishing it. Inputs: `python-version` (default `""`, which leaves `UV_PYTHON` unset and lets uv pick), `shinylive-version` (default `"shinylive"`, for pinning), and `app-dir` (default `"."`).
- **`examples/deploy-app.yaml`** — what users copy into their own repo; calls the above at `@actions/v1` and grants `pages: write` / `id-token: write`.
- **`examples/README.md`** plus a README "GitHub Pages" section documenting the contract.

The Python workflow is simpler than the R one because it needs no dependency-discovery step. `shinylive export` reads the app's own `requirements.txt` and records those packages in `app.json` for Pyodide to install in the browser, so nothing app-specific is installed on the runner. The runner's Python only runs the exporter — the Pyodide Python version comes from the shinylive web assets — which is why there is no pinned `python-version` default.

### Self-test

r-shinylive does not exercise its own reusable workflow anywhere, so this adds one. `.github/workflows/test-deploy-app.yaml` calls the branch's copy of `deploy-app.yaml` against a small fixture app in `tests/app/`, with `shinylive-version: "."` so the exporter is built from the checkout rather than pulled from PyPI. Changes to the workflow are therefore validated before the `actions/v1` tag is moved onto them.

It triggers on `pull_request` only. `github.ref` is then `refs/pull/N/merge`, never `refs/heads/main`, so the gated upload/deploy steps stay skipped and this repository's own GitHub Pages is never touched.

The fixture depends on `faicons` so the export also covers the case where a package comes from the app's `requirements.txt` rather than base Pyodide. It is excluded from pyright (`pyrightconfig.json`) and flake8 (`setup.cfg`) because it imports packages that are not dependencies of this repo.

**Follow-up required before this is usable by others:** the `actions/v1` tag must be created and force-moved after merge, the same way r-shinylive maintains it. `examples/deploy-app.yaml` currently references a ref that does not exist.

## Verification

Ran the exact command the workflow runs, then loaded the result in a browser:

```bash
uvx --from '.' shinylive export 'tests/app' /tmp/sitecheck
uv run --no-project python -m http.server --directory /tmp/sitecheck --bind 127.0.0.1 8017
```

The app renders and is reactive, with 0 console errors. The gear icon confirms `faicons` was installed in Pyodide from `requirements.txt`:


`actionlint` passes on all three workflow files. `black --check .`, `isort --check-only .`, and `flake8 shinylive tests` pass; `pyright` reports no diagnostics under `tests/app`.

title: ci: Check that PR titles follow Conventional Commits
description:
Builds on posit-dev/py-shinylive#87. Adds shinyreact's pull request title check.

## Changes

- New `.github/workflows/pr-title.yaml` runs `amannn/action-semantic-pull-request` with shinyreact's types: `build`, `chore`, `ci`, `docs`, `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `release`, `style`, `test`. All recent titles on `main`, including `release: v0.8.13`, already pass.
- When a title fails, a sticky comment explains the format. It is deleted once the title is fixed.
- Unlike shinyreact, it runs on `pull_request_target` instead of `pull_request`. Pull requests from forks get a read-only token under `pull_request`, so the comment step would fail and turn the check red even for a good title. The job never checks out the pull request's code, so `pull_request_target` is safe here.
- The memory bank lists the new workflow.

`pull_request_target` runs the workflow file from the base branch, so this check starts running on pull requests only after it merges.

title: build: Tidy the Makefile and add pre-commit hooks
description:
Builds on posit-dev/py-shinylive#86. Follows shinyreact's conventions.

## Changes

- **Makefile:**
  - Each target prints an emoji progress line (🧪 tests, 📝 types, 🔍 lint, 📐 format, 🧳 build, 🧹 clean).
  - `make help` uses shinyreact's `grep`/`awk` approach with colored target names, so it no longer needs Python. `make coverage` opens the report with `python -m webbrowser`, so the embedded Python scripts are gone.
  - Every target has its own `.PHONY` line.
  - `make setup` replaces `make install-deps`: it runs `uv sync --upgrade` and `pre-commit install`.
  - The `clean-*` helpers are no longer listed in `make help`; `make clean` still runs them.
- **pre-commit:** `.pre-commit-config.yaml` adds shinyreact's hooks: trailing whitespace, end of file, `check-yaml`, merge conflicts, large files, `ruff-check`, and `ruff-format`. `pre-commit` is added to the `dev` group. All hooks pass on the current files.
- **CI:** step names in `build.yml` get the same emojis as shinyreact's workflows.
- **CI job name:** the `build` job in `build.yml` is renamed to `check`, so it does not share a name with `deploy-app / build`. This is the name to require for auto-merge.
- **Docs:** `AGENTS.md` and the memory bank are updated. The memory bank notes that git worktrees share one hooks folder, so `pre-commit install` in one worktree affects all of them.

title: build: Test all Python versions with tox in one CI job
description:
Builds on posit-dev/py-shinylive#85. Last PR in the build tooling stack: pyproject.toml → uv → ruff → pyrefly → **tox**.

## Changes

- **tox:** `[tool.tox]` in `pyproject.toml` defines `py310` to `py314`, set up like shinyreact. `tox` and `tox-uv` are in the `dev` group, and tox-uv downloads any missing Python versions. tox builds the wheel once and installs it in each environment with a new `test` dependency group (only pytest). The `dev` group includes `test`, so `uv sync` still installs everything.
- **Tests now really use the wheel.** pytest's default import mode puts the repo root first on `sys.path`, so the old CI step (`make install`, then `make test`) still imported `shinylive/` from the source folder. tox runs pytest with `--import-mode=importlib`, and the tests import the installed wheel.
- **Asset tests still skip in CI.** They skip when `CI` is `true` and the event is not a release. tox does not pass environment variables on by default, so `pass_env` adds `CI` and `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`. Without it, every PR downloaded the assets once per Python version, all into the same cache folder.
- **CI:** the five-job Python matrix is now one `build` job: `uv sync`, `make test-all`, `make check`. `UV_NO_SYNC` and the `make install` step are no longer needed. `main` has no required status checks, so the renamed job blocks nothing.
- **Makefile:** a new `make test-all` runs `uv run tox run-parallel`.
- **Docs:** `AGENTS.md` and the memory bank are updated. This also fixes a garbled line in `memory-bank/ciAndTooling.md` from posit-dev/py-shinylive#82.

## Speed

On this PR's CI run, the single job took about 18 seconds from start to finish. The matrix also took about 17 seconds, since its five jobs ran at the same time on separate runners. Results come back just as fast, and the total runner time drops from about 75 to about 18 seconds. On a laptop, `make test-all` takes about 6 seconds the first time and about 2 seconds after that.

title: build: Replace pyright with pyrefly
description:
Builds on posit-dev/py-shinylive#84. Part of the build tooling stack: pyproject.toml → uv → ruff → **pyrefly** → tox.

## Changes

- **Tool:** pyrefly replaces pyright in the `dev` group, as in py-shiny. `pyrightconfig.json` is removed; settings are in `[tool.pyrefly]` with py-shiny's `infer-with-first-use = false` and errors for `implicit-any` and `unused-ignore`. py-shiny's global `no-access = "ignore"` is left out, because pyrefly finds no such errors here. `tests/app` stays excluded.
- **Fixes for pyrefly's errors (no baseline needed):**
  - The `verbose_print` defaults were `lambda *args: None`, whose parameter type is unknown. They now use a typed `print_nothing()` in `_utils.py`.
  - `files = []` in `_deps.py` is now `files.clear()`. It empties the same `os.walk()` list, so the behavior is unchanged.
  - `FAKE_LOCK` in `tests/conftest.py` gets a type.
  - Two needless `str()` and `int()` calls are removed.
- **Stubs:** `types-chevron` is added to the `dev` group. pyright bundled these stubs; pyrefly does not.
- **Comments:** the `# pyright: ignore` comments are removed. pyrefly reports no error at any of those lines.
- **`# type: ignore` comments with pyright rule names** are gone too. In `tests/test_assets_version.py`, a `read_saved()` helper checks for `None`, and two test doubles get real types. The only ignores left are `# pyrefly: ignore[untyped-import]` on the two `lzstring` imports, since that package has no stubs.
- **Dead branch:** `read_app_files()` compared `rel_dir` (a `Path`) to `"."`, which is never true. pyright flagged this and the old code silenced it. The branch is removed; `Path(".") / name` already gives `name`.
- `make pyrefly` replaces `make pyright`; `make check`, the CI step name, `AGENTS.md`, and the memory bank are updated.

pyright ran in strict mode. pyrefly's defaults check less in some areas (for example, unknown member types), so a few problems pyright would have caught may now pass.

title: build: Replace black, flake8, and isort with ruff
description:
Builds on posit-dev/py-shinylive#82. Part of the build tooling stack: pyproject.toml → uv → **ruff** → pyrefly → tox.

## Changes

- **Tools:** ruff replaces black, isort, flake8, and flake8-bugbear in the `dev` group. `.flake8` and `[tool.isort]` are removed.
- **Rules:** `select = ["E", "F", "I", "B"]` at line length 88. `B` keeps the flake8-bugbear checks the repo had before. `E501` stays off, as it was for flake8, because `ruff format` already wraps code and only long strings and comments remain.
- **`B904` fix:** `bundle_from_url()` in `_url.py` now raises its `ValueError` with `from e`, so the original decode error is kept.
- **Star import:** `tests/test_url.py` now imports `FileContentJson`, `ShinyliveApp`, and `url_decode` by name, so the old `F403`/`F405` ignores are gone.
- **Makefile:** `make lint` runs `ruff check`, `make check` adds `ruff format --check`, and a new `make format` runs `ruff check --fix` and `ruff format`.
- **Editor and docs:** `.vscode/settings.json` uses the ruff formatter; `AGENTS.md`, the memory bank, and the CI step name are updated.

No code is reformatted: ruff's formatter and import sorting match the current black and isort output.

title: build: Use uv in the Makefile and CI
description:
Builds on posit-dev/py-shinylive#48. Part of the build tooling stack: pyproject.toml → **uv** → ruff → pyrefly → tox.

## Changes

- **Dev dependencies:** the `dev` and `test` extras become one `dev` dependency group. `uv sync` and `uv run` install it by default, and it no longer appears in the published package metadata.
- **Makefile:** every tool runs through `uv run`, so no activated environment is needed. `make dist` uses `uv build` (no `hatch` CLI), `make release` uses `uv publish`, `make install` uses `uv pip install`, and a new `make install-deps` runs `uv sync`. `make help` now calls `python3`, since `python` is missing on some systems.
- **CI:** `build.yml` uses `astral-sh/setup-uv` (pinned like `deploy-app.yaml`) and `uv sync` in place of `setup-python` and pip. The build job sets `UV_NO_SYNC=1` so that `uv run` does not replace the wheel from `make install` with the editable copy.
- **`uv.lock`** is ignored so CI keeps testing the newest dependencies, as users get them.
- `AGENTS.md`, the memory bank, and `CHANGELOG.md` are updated.

r-shinylive needs no matching change; this only affects how the Python package is built.

title: fix: Address bugs and doc errors found by the memory bank
description: Fixes the "Behavior", "Docs", and "Tests and CI" items in [posit-dev/py-shinylive#81](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/81). Each commit fixes one area, and each code fix adds a test that failed before the fix (except the Windows-only encoding fixes, which can't fail on macOS or Linux). Adapted from [posit-dev/r-shinylive#217](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/217). Code fixes: - **Export:** - Keep the app and the export in separate folders, like `shinylive export myapp site`. A `DESTDIR` equal to `APPDIR` (`export . .`) or holding it (`export myapp .`) is now an error instead of an empty `app.json`. A `DESTDIR` inside `APPDIR` still works, and is left out of the app. - Paths are compared with a new `comparable_path()` (absolute, symlinks resolved, `normcase`), so mixed relative/absolute paths are handled. It is only used to compare paths, never to name files. - Files in `app.json` are sorted, so the order is the same on every run. - A new `check_subdir()` rejects `..` and treats `.` as no subdir. Nested `--subdir` and `DESTDIR` folders are created. - `path_length()` counts parts on Windows. - All messages go to stderr, including `--verbose` ones. `--verbose` now also lists packages not found in the lock. Template pages and `app.json` are written as UTF-8. - **CLI:** a `--template-params` JSON string longer than a file name can be works on Python 3.10 to 3.13. `assets remove --help` loses a stray `"`. - **Assets:** `install-from-local` checks `BUILD` before removing the installed version. Download progress shows only the MB so far when the server sends no size. `_check_assets_url()`, which only a release test used, moves into that test. - **Pyodide packages:** relative imports are skipped. `requirements.txt` option lines, local paths, VCS URLs, and inline comments are skipped. Base files and package dependencies are sorted. - **`ShinyliveApp`:** folders in `files` are added (and the app file is skipped if a folder holds it); a folder outside the app folder, or any folder for an app from text, keeps its name (`www/s.css`) like `add_dir()`; `add_file(overwrite=True)` replaces; `remove_file()` and `-` remove; files can mix relative and absolute paths, and a file outside the app folder can be added with a name; names always use `/`; `write_files()` creates subfolders, writes UTF-8, and refuses names outside the folder; URLs on other hosts decode with the right language and mode. Docs, tests, and tooling: - README, `examples/README.md`, CLI help, and docstring errors are fixed. - A new `fake_assets` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` makes a tiny offline assets cache, so export and package code can be tested without the network. New tests cover export, the CLI, assets, packages, and `ShinyliveApp` files. - `make test-all` (no tox config) is removed; `coverage` is a dev dependency for `make coverage`. Deprecated `setup.cfg` keys are replaced or removed. The Python 3.8 `is_relative_to()` wrapper is removed. CHANGELOG bullets are added, and the memory-bank docs now match the new behavior. Not changed: the "Possibly by design" items in the issue (`\r\n` read as `\n`, local modules named like packages, re-export keeps old asset files, scripts also listed as resources, asset tests that run locally without opt-in, `appdirs`). The "On push events" comment in `.github/workflows/deploy-app.yaml` is left alone, so that the `actions/v1` tag does not need to move. r-shinylive: these fixes are Python-only or already fixed in [posit-dev/r-shinylive#217](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/217). Nothing shared with r-shinylive (the `extension` JSON shape, the cache folder, `versions.json`) changes, except that resource lists are now sorted. --- Stack created with GitHub Stacks CLI • Give Feedback 💬

title: fix: Time out stalled downloads and keep mirror downloads offline
description:
## Summary

Third PR in the stack for [posit-dev/py-shinylive#69](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/69); builds on [posit-dev/py-shinylive#72](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/72). Follow-ups from review that did not fit in [posit-dev/py-shinylive#72](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/72).

* **Mirror downloads stay offline.** `ensure_shinylive_assets(url=...)` never contacts GitHub. It chooses the version from `versions.json` and the downloaded folders. For a series or `"latest"`, the tarball may hold a newer matching version than the one chosen, and that folder is used. An exact version must still match the tarball's folder.
* **Downloads time out.** A download that gets no data for 60 seconds fails instead of hanging forever (for example, during a Quarto render). A slow download that keeps receiving data still finishes. The temp file is removed on failure.
* **A bad `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` is a usage error.** `export` (without `--assets-version`), the `assets` commands, and the `extension` commands report it as a usage error instead of a traceback. `assets cleanup` also rejects it.

title: feat!: Float the Shinylive assets version within a series
description:
## Summary

Closes [posit-dev/py-shinylive#69](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/69). Second of two PRs; builds on [posit-dev/py-shinylive#71](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/71). This matches [posit-dev/r-shinylive#218](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/218), so a Quarto document with both `shinylive-python` and `shinylive-r` blocks keeps rendering when a new assets patch release comes out.

* **Default is a series.** Assets helpers take `version=None` and use `assets_version()`: the newest release in `0.10.*`, unless `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` is set. Before, py-shinylive ignored that env var.
* **Quarto.** `extension info` checks GitHub and downloads the version it reports, so its `codeblock-to-json` script path exists. `base-htmldeps`, `language-resources`, and `app-resources` only read the `versions.json` that `info` just saved, so one render uses one version, and R (which shares the file) picks the same one.
* **`versions.json` only names downloaded versions.** A GitHub check is saved only once the chosen version is downloaded. If that download fails and an older local version is used, the saved file leaves out the newer releases of that series, clears `latest` (so the next check gets the full list), and records the error (so the next check runs within an hour). Calls that only read (`check=False`) never write it. R needs the same rule: [posit-dev/r-shinylive#223](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/223).
* **CLI.**
  * `shinylive export --assets-version` is new.
  * `assets download --version` accepts a series or `latest`.
  * Bad version inputs (`--assets-version`, `--version`, `--keep`) give a usage error.
  * `assets cleanup --keep` is new. By default it keeps the newest downloaded version of the default series and of `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION`, and it removes temp files older than 10 minutes left by interrupted downloads.
  * `assets info` shows the version in use, the default series, and the last check, without using the network.
  * `assets version` prints the version that will be used, without downloading.
  * The `shinylive` help header shows the series instead of one version.
  * `assets install-from-local` and `link-from-local` name the build after the version in the `package.json` of the shinylive repository that holds it (unless `--version` is given, which must be an exact version), and print how to use it (`SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION=<v>`).
* **Downloads** extract to a temp folder (made after the download finishes, so cleanup never removes a slow download) and move into place. A re-download moves the old folder aside, moves the new one in, and only then deletes the old one. If another process (R or Python) just finished the same download, its folder is kept. The temp names (`extract-`, `old-`, `versions-`) match R, so either package's cleanup removes them.
* **`ensure_shinylive_assets(url=...)`** downloads a missing folder from `url`, never from GitHub, and errors if the tarball has no `shinylive-<version>` folder. `url` and `version` are documented on `download_shinylive()` and `ensure_shinylive_assets()`.
* **`shinylive._version.SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION`** now gives a `FutureWarning`: it is the fallback version, not the version in use.
* README and CHANGELOG updated.

**Behavior change:** the assets version is no longer constant. It can change over time, and resolving it may use the network or download assets. Pin an exact version for builds that must repeat exactly.

## TODO

- [x] Match the `versions.json` save rule in R: [posit-dev/r-shinylive#223](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/223).
- [ ] Match the review follow-ups ([posit-dev/py-shinylive#71](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/71), [posit-dev/py-shinylive#76](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/76)) in R: [posit-dev/r-shinylive#225](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/225).
- [ ] The reusable `deploy-app` workflow could gain an `assets-version` input: [posit-dev/py-shinylive#74](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/74).
- [ ] After release, open PRs to the two known users of `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION`: [posit-dev/py-shinylive#75](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/75).

title: feat: Add Shinylive assets version resolution
description:
## Summary

First of two PRs for [posit-dev/py-shinylive#69](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/69). It adds `shinylive/_assets_version.py`, which turns a version input into one exact Shinylive assets version. Nothing uses it yet; [posit-dev/py-shinylive#72](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/72) wires it in.

It follows `R/assets_version.R` from [posit-dev/r-shinylive#218](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/218):

* **Inputs:** an exact version (`"0.10.16"`), a series (`"0.10.*"`), or `"latest"`. A non-`None` argument beats the `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` env var, which beats the default series. An empty env var counts as unset. A bad env var gives an error that names it.
* **Constants:** `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION_DEFAULT = "0.10.*"` and `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION_FALLBACK = "0.10.16"`. `SHINYLIVE_ASSETS_VERSION` stays as an alias of the fallback for code that imports it ([posit-dev/py-shinylive#72](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/72) makes it warn).
* **`versions.json`:** same file and format as R, in the same cache folder, so both packages choose the same version. Checked at most once a day, once an hour after a failed check, and every time for `"latest"`. The check is a HEAD request to `releases/latest` (not the API). The full release list (GitHub API, uses `GITHUB_PAT` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` if set, and retries without the token after a 401) is only fetched when the latest tag changes. Failures keep the old list. Written to a temp file and renamed. A read-only cache is tolerated: when the file can't be saved, the check returns what is saved, so later `check=False` calls choose the same version. ([posit-dev/py-shinylive#72](https://github.com/posit-dev/py-shinylive/issues/72) replaces this: a check is saved only once the chosen version is downloaded, and a read-only cache just skips the save.)
* **Resolution:** highest match from the release list and the downloaded folders. Offline: the highest downloaded match (with a warning that says when the check failed, why, and when GitHub is checked again; it repeats in every process until then), then the fallback version, then a clear error (which also says why the fallback download failed). A failed download falls back the same way. An exact version is downloaded too, and a failed download of it is an error. `check=False` reads only `versions.json`; `download=False` never downloads. Warnings point at the first caller outside the package.
* **One version per process:** `assets_version()` resolves once and then returns the same value. `set_assets_version()` sets it and clears the cached Pyodide package data in `_deps`.

title: docs(agents): Add AGENTS.md with r-shinylive sync steps
description:
## Summary

Adds an `AGENTS.md` for coding agents: a short project overview, the development commands, two conventions (CHANGELOG bullets, and keeping stdout clean for the Quarto extension), and a "Keep r-shinylive in sync" section.

That section lists what the Python and R packages share (the Quarto extension commands and JSON, the assets cache folder and `versions.json`, and how the assets version is chosen). It asks contributors to check whether each feature or bug fix also needs an r-shinylive change, and to open a linked issue or PR there.

The matching r-shinylive change is [posit-dev/r-shinylive#219](https://github.com/posit-dev/r-shinylive/issues/219).
